messages.content: What is a museum for?
A museum keeps things so people can meet them again. It is a long conversation between makers and lookers. What would you put in a museum of your own life?
Why do paintings crack?
Paint shrinks and the canvas moves with the weather. Over centuries those small movements become a web of cracks. Have you noticed how the cracks follow the brushstrokes?
What is a sketchbook good for?
A sketchbook is a place to be wrong in private. Most good ideas start as bad drawings there. What did you last draw without showing anyone?
How should I look at an abstract painting?
Stand close, then far, and notice what changes. Let colour and edge do the talking before you look for a subject. Which part of it pulls your eye first?
What is typography?
Typography is the craft of making words visible. It decides how a sentence sounds before anyone reads it. Which typeface do you trust without knowing why?
Why are museums so quiet?
Quiet lets small details become loud. It is also a habit left from older ideas of reverence. Do you think a museum should be noisier?
What makes a good photograph?
A good photograph is a decision about what to leave out. Light and timing do the rest. What is outside the frame of your favourite photo?
What is a curator?
A curator chooses, arranges and explains. The choices are an argument made with objects instead of words. What argument would your first exhibition make?
Is graffiti art?
Graffiti is art that refuses to ask permission. Some of it is careful and some of it is a shout. Which wall in your town would you change?
What is colour theory?
Colour theory describes how colours change each other. A grey looks warm beside blue and cool beside orange. Have you ever been fooled by a colour?
How do I start a creative project?
Start smaller than feels serious. Make one rough version before you plan the perfect one. What is the smallest piece you could make today?
What is the Bauhaus?
The Bauhaus was a German school that joined art, craft and industry. Its teachers wanted chairs and posters to be as considered as paintings. Which object near you looks like it came from there?
Why do artists make self-portraits?
A self-portrait is the one model that is always available. It is also a way to study change over a lifetime. How would you draw yourself without your face?
What is a moodboard?
A moodboard collects images that share a feeling before a project has a shape. It helps a team agree on a direction without words. What would be on a moodboard for this week?
What is design?
Design is deciding on purpose. It is the plan behind how something looks, works and feels. What everyday object do you think is badly designed?
How old is the oldest art?
Some cave markings and shell carvings are more than forty thousand years old. People have been making images for as long as we can trace. What do you think the first artist wanted to say?
What is negative space?
Negative space is the shape of the empty part. Designers use it to make the full parts clearer. Can you see the arrow hidden in a well known delivery logo?
Why do we restore old artworks?
Restoration slows decay and removes later damage. It is also a choice about which past to keep. Should a restorer ever add what is missing?
What is a print?
A print is an image made to be repeated, from a block, plate or screen. Each copy is an original of a kind. Would you rather own a print or a unique drawing?
What is performance art?
Performance art uses a body and time as its material. It happens once, and what remains is memory and documentation. What would you do for an hour in front of strangers?
